rounds.proof_sketch: With N=4096, row∈[0,4095], the mutation changes write target from row*N+col to row/N+col=0+col=col. Both paths write constant 0.0f. Output matrix C is initialized to zeros via torch::zeros(). Upper triangular positions (col>row) were never computed and remain 0 regardless of whether original writes 0 to C[row,col] or mutant writes 0 to C[0,col]. All affected positions start at 0 and end at 0.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation affects only the else branch where col > row (upper triangular region). In the original code, this branch explicitly writes 0 to C[row, col]. In the mutated code, it writes 0 to C[col] (C[0, col] in 2D). However, since the output tensor is initialized with torch::zeros, all positions start at 0. The upper triangular positions are never touched by the lower triangular computation, so they remain 0 regardless of whether the explicit zeroing writes to the correct location or not. Both versions produce identical all-zero upper triangular outputs.
rounds.kill_strategy: The mutant is unkillable because the mutation only affects where a redundant write of 0 goes. Since the output is zero-initialized and the affected code path writes constant 0 (not derived from input values), no input values can cause distinguishable behavior.
rounds.recommendations: Avoid redundant explicit zeroing of pre-initialized memory; this creates equivalent mutants when the zeroing statement is modified. If explicit zeroing is needed for clarity, consider adding a comment explaining it's redundant but intentional for safety, which could help mutation testing tools recognize such patterns.
